_comment: POST-CHECKPOINT EXECUTION CONTRACT. Frozen 2026-09-21. The executing agent makes NO decisions during recovery: every value it needs is stated here or in the baseline. Any deviation is a STOP, not a judgement call.

blocked_until.checkpoint_rule: the FIRST APPLICABLE CLEANUP SWEEP AFTER that moment — not the moment itself
blocked_until.note: No rebuild may start before this resolves. A pre-checkpoint rebuild multiplies exposure if KEEP does not hold.

control.when: BEFORE the first rebuild and AFTER every single recovery

recovery_order.rationale: configuration twin of the proven control

excluded.instruction: DO NOT REBUILD. Deletion is not authorized either; P0-4 has its own gate.

execution_rule: ONE service at a time. rebuild -> run all 9 assertions -> re-verify control -> STOP on any failure. Do not batch. Do not proceed to order N+1 until order N is completely green.

assertions.text: the new revision carries 100% of traffic

BLOCKED: scaling configuration must be owner-adjudicated before this candidate is rebuilt. This assertion no longer states an expected value, because the correct value is an unresolved product decision, not a fact the repository can supply.
assertions.note: Do not replace this with `minInstances: 1` merely because that is what the source now says. Encoding the newly discovered source state would prematurely decide cold-start latency versus ~708 billable instance-hours per service per month.
assertions.retracted_note: the P0-3 result; already minInstanceCount=0 at the function layer, so the rebuild MATERIALISES it rather than setting it
assertions.retraction: The previous assertion — that the recovery candidates carried minInstanceCount=0 and that a rebuild would MATERIALISE that rather than set it — was based SOLELY on the GCF layer. It did not inspect source configuration or the serving revision. Source inspection establishes `minInstances: 1` for all six candidates, with explicit latency rationale written into the code, while the serving revisions are pinned at minScale=1. A rebuild would therefore RESTORE the pin, not remove it — reinstating the cost configuration P0-3 set out to eliminate.

assertions.text: the new image digest is present in Artifact Registry
the previously stuck failed revision is no longer latestCreatedRevisionName and is therefore deletable
FULL STRUCTURAL EQUALITY of the trigger specification, pre vs post
assertions.method: compare baseline entry `raw` against a fresh describe, after deterministic key ordering only. NO field may be selected away, added, removed, changed or silently normalised. A rebuild must reproduce the trigger CONTRACT, not something resembling it.
assertions.applies: all six; DECISIVE for onOrderStatusChange and onNewOrderCreated

assertions.text: memory, cpu, timeout, concurrency, ingress and service account match the baseline exactly

assertions.note: exact equality, not approximate. A creation, deletion or name collision FAILS the gate.

assertions.text: the control (profilegetpublicprofile) still satisfies every condition in `control.must_hold`

authorization.first_rebuild: NOT AUTHORIZED — additionally BLOCKED by scaling_contract_adjudication until the owner decisions are made and this manifest is re-certified.
authorization.note: This manifest is a contract, not a permission. Each execution step needs its own authorization.

scaling_contract_invariant: A rebuild may NOT proceed when source and serving scaling configuration differ, unless the difference carries an explicit owner adjudication. This catches both directions: source absent with production set (processTypesenseQueue: repo declared no maxInstances, production had 80, the rebuild REMOVED it), and source set with production matching (the six: source min=1, serving min=1 — which is NOT automatically safe, because the value itself is disputed by P0-3).

scaling_contract_adjudication.method: read-only: source grep at each declaration site, gcloud functions describe, gcloud run revisions describe on the SERVING revision
scaling_contract_adjudication.observability_note: The GCF layer reports minInstanceCount=undefined for all seven while BOTH the source and the serving revision say 1. The GCF layer is the representation that agrees with neither — it is an observability discrepancy, NOT evidence that the functions are unpinned. The serving revision is the authoritative statement of what is actually running.

rows.detail: maxInstances=80 existed in production outside repository authority. The 2026-09-21 rebuild removed it; the ceiling is now unset. Decide whether 80 becomes source-authoritative or unbounded scaling is intended.
The only candidate whose source declares BOTH values and matches its serving revision. Still HELD: the manifest itself must be re-certified first.

decisions_required: MINIMUM — is the explicit `minInstances: 1` latency requirement still intended despite P0-3's cost finding? The source argues it is; P0-3 argues the opposite. The repository cannot settle this by having been edited more recently.
MAXIMUM — what ceiling should replace the externally maintained 80/99 values, and should it become source-authoritative? Six of seven never declare one, so every rebuild removes one.
TYPESENSE — should processTypesenseQueue's former external maxInstances=80 become source-authoritative, or is unbounded scaling intended?
